page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance belonging to the ecs.se1ne family, utilizing the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with 16 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 architecture, powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The system features 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. The processor supports AVX and AVX-512F instruction sets, alongside AES cryptography and FMA extensions.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance profile characterized by moderate multi-threaded capabilities paired with weak single-core performance. The single-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores fall into the bottom 25% and 10% respectively, reflecting the lower clock speed and older architecture of the Intel Xeon 8269CY. However, multi-core benchmarks, such as multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench multi-core tests, reach average tiers. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate average throughput, though the Passmark memory score is weak. Database operations and Redis SET performance remain in the average tier, processing 11.19 million operations per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.se1ne.4xlarge offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not require high single-threaded compute performance. The lack of bundled local storage and GPUs makes it a specialized choice for memory-intensive applications. It is best suited for workloads such as database operations, caching layers, static web serving, and moderate multi-threaded tasks like software compilation or text processing, where memory capacity is prioritized over raw CPU speed.
